Here is the full analysis.\n\n# Root cause\n\n`SegmentImpl::flush()` decides whether there is anything to persist by checking the **in-process WAL member handle** (`wal_file_`), not the actual data state (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:2217-2222`). After a pure WAL-replay recovery, that handle is `nullptr` even though the segment holds N never-persisted documents, so the flush inside `Optimize()`'s segment switch silently no-ops — and the optimize then rewrites the manifest in a way that demotes the segment to \"persisted\" with zero persisted blocks and orphans the WAL file that held the only durable copy.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Recovery path vs. ordinary insertion path\n\n**Ordinary insertion.** `SegmentImpl::Insert` (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903-918`) calls `append_wal` **first** (`:4324-4340`), which lazily opens the member `wal_file_` via `open_wal_file()` (`:4303-4322`) and appends the record; only then `internal_insert` (`:837-881`) writes the in-memory forward store, id map, indexers, `doc_ids_`, and the writing-block meta (`max_doc_id_`, `doc_count_`, `:874-878`). So after inserts, the segment has **both** dirty memory data **and** an open WAL handle with records (`has_record()` = file larger than header, `src/db/index/storage/wal/local_wal_file.h:75-77`).\n\n**Recovery path.** `CollectionImpl::Open` → `recovery()` (`src/db/collection.cc:1836-1892`) loads the manifest and re-opens the writing segment from `v.writing_segment_meta()` (`:1879-1887`). `SegmentImpl::Open` sees a `writing_forward_block` in the meta and calls `recover()` (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:484-501`). `recover()` (`:4193-4301`) opens the WAL into a **local** handle `recover_wal_file` (`:4206-4214`), closes it at scope exit via `AILEGO_DEFER` (`:4215`), and replays each record through `internal_insert/update/upsert/delete` (`:4249-4272`) — the `internal_*` methods never call `append_wal`. **The member `wal_file_` is never assigned during recovery.**\n\n**Why the data is initially readable.** Replay populates exactly the in-memory structures the read path uses: `memory_store_->insert(doc)` (`:857`), `id_map_->upsert` (`:853`), scalar/FTS/vector indexers (`:861-872`), and `doc_ids_.push_back` (`:878`). `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` minus filtered deletes (`:589-599`), and `CollectionImpl::Stats` sums per-segment `doc_count` (`src/db/collection.cc:403-429`). So counting and fetching work entirely from memory.\n\nThe distinguishing state, therefore: after recovery the segment is **dirty** (N docs existing only in memory + an on-disk WAL referenced by the current manifest's writing block), yet it looks **clean** to any code keyed on `wal_file_`.\n\n*Secondary observation (source-reading only):* `recover()` also does `mem_block.max_doc_id_ += added_docs` (`:4285-4288`) after `internal_insert` has already set `max_doc_id_` to the last allocated id (`:875`). That appears to double-count, inflating the next segment's `min_doc_id` (`src/db/collection.cc:1527-1531`) — a doc-id gap, but **not** the loss mechanism. Confirming its runtime effect would require execution.\n\n## 2. Call sequence and exact condition for the silent success\n\n1. `CollectionImpl::Optimize` (`src/db/collection.cc:779-915`) checks `writing_segment_->doc_count() != 0` (`:794`) — true (N recovered docs) — and calls `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` (`:1517-1552`).\n2. That calls `writing_segment_->dump()` (`:1519`) → `SegmentImpl::dump` (`segment.cc:2197-2215`) → `flush()` (`:2201`).\n3. **The exact condition:** `flush()`'s guard at `segment.cc:2220-2222`:\n   ```cpp\n   if (wal_file_ == nullptr || !wal_file_->has_record()) {\n     return Status::OK();\n   }\n   ```\n   `wal_file_` is `nullptr` (never attached during recovery), so flush returns OK **without** doing any of: `memory_store_->flush()` (`:2233-2236`), `finish_memory_components()` (`:2288-2298` → `:4342-4412`, the *only* place the in-memory block becomes a persisted `BlockMeta`), `update_version()` (`:2300-2302` → `:4414-4426`), or WAL removal (`:2304-2315`). `dump()` then seals and returns OK (`:2204-2214`).\n4. Back in `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`, trusting the OK: the old segment is added to the persist-segment manager (`collection.cc:1522`), a new empty writing segment is created (`:1527-1531`), and the manifest is rewritten: old meta `remove_writing_forward_block()` (`:1537-1538`; `src/db/index/common/meta.h:263-265`), `add_persisted_segment_meta` (`:1539`), `reset_writing_segment_meta` (`:1543`), `apply` + `flush` (`:1546-1549`). `VersionManager::flush` writes a new manifest file and **deletes the previous one** (`src/db/index/common/version_manager.cc:282-301`). This is the point of no return: the old segment's persisted meta now contains **zero forward blocks** (step 3 skipped `finish_memory_components`) and **no writing block** (so no WAL path is derivable from it anymore).
